references.text: The expression "came to himself" (εἰς ἑαυτὸν ἐλθών) describes a turning point where the prodigal son realizes his situation. This is a moment of repentance and self-awareness that is central to the parable.

"Let us examine our ways and test them, and let us return to the Lord" ([ref:Klag 3:40|Lamentations 3:40]). The same pattern of self-awareness and repentance that the prodigal son goes through when he "comes to himself."

"When he turns from all his transgressions and repents" ([ref:Esek 18:28|Ezekiel 18:28]). Ezekiel describes the same turning point where a person recognizes their sin and decides to turn back, just as the prodigal son does.

"For after I turned away, I repented; and after I came to my senses, I struck my thigh" ([ref:Jer 31:19|Jeremiah 31:19]). Ephraim's repentance and turning back reflect the prodigal son's self-awareness and decision to return to his father.

The prodigal son's realization in verse 17 leads directly to his decision to get up, go to his father, and confess his sin ([ref:Luk 15:18-19|Luke 15:18-19]). Self-awareness leads to concrete action and repentance.
The demon-possessed man who was healed was found "in his right mind" (σωφρονοῦντα) at Jesus' feet ([ref:Luk 8:35|Luke 8:35]). To "come to oneself" is parallel to being restored to a rational state.

Solomon's prayer that the people in captivity should "turn their hearts," repent, and pray ([ref:1 Kong 8:47-48|1 Kings 8:47-48]). The same movement from recognizing sin to repentance as seen with the prodigal son.

"I was foolish and understood nothing; I was like a beast before you" ([ref:Sal 73:22|Psalm 73:22]). The psalmist acknowledges his former ignorance, just as the prodigal son recognizes that even his father's hired workers have more than he does.

"Why do you spend money on what is not bread, and your labor on what does not satisfy?" ([ref:Jes 55:2|Isaiah 55:2]). The prodigal son realizes he is starving while his father's hired workers have plenty of food—a contrast between the empty life away from God and the abundance found with the Father.

Paul's mission to open people's eyes so they may turn from darkness to light ([ref:Apg 26:18-20|Acts 26:18-20]). The prodigal son's repentance is an example of the pattern Jesus calls people to: coming to awareness and turning back to God.
